title: teranode-bridge
description: Landing-tier shim for pushed delivery into an unmodified Teranode cluster. Metric names and histogram buckets match Teranode's own, so bridge and cluster series can share a panel.

panels.title: Echo mismatches
panels.description: Objects that returned on the delivery lanes with DIFFERENT bytes than were published. An object-plane data-integrity fault, never expected to be non-zero.

panels.title: Submitters active
panels.description: Must be EXACTLY 1 per cluster per class. 0 means nothing is published upward; 2 means double publish. Scope $job/$instance to one cluster's bridges or this reads high.

panels.title: Cluster FSM
panels.description: Read over the reverse path's blockchain connection. Advisory: the bridge announces and submits identically whatever state the cluster is in.

panels.title: Cluster height
panels.description: The cluster's best block header height, as the cluster reports it.

panels.title: Announce backlog
panels.description: Records the Kafka client still holds unproduced. A sustained non-zero level is a BACKLOG, not a failure — the failure counter stays flat while objects the cluster has not been told about pile up.

panels.title: Awaiting pull
panels.description: Announcements acked but not yet pulled. Climbing means announcements land and pulls do not follow — check -advertise, -api-prefix and the topic names.

panels.title: Objects read
panels.description: Whole objects read off each delivery lane.

panels.title: Connections open
panels.description: Zero on a lane that should be fed is a whole-edge outage — a condition no counter can show, because a dead edge stops incrementing rather than reporting.

panels.title: Lane faults
panels.description: dropped = framing fault (the connection goes, there is no resync point). rejected = well-framed but wrong format, a sender bug. errors = handler failure.

panels.title: Object size p99
panels.description: The bytes counter gives the mean; only this gives the shape. Off on the tx lane unless -tx-size-histogram is set.

panels.title: Cache occupancy
panels.description: Against the -cache-bytes ceiling. Eviction is expected under load; it is only a problem paired with retrieval misses.

panels.title: Announcements
panels.description: Failures mean the object stays cached but the cluster never learns of it.

panels.title: Announce → first pull
panels.description: THE bridge SLI. Nothing on either side measures it — the cluster does not know when it was told, the fabric does not know when the cluster acted. A rising p99 means the cache TTL will start evicting objects before they are fetched.

panels.title: Pulls served
panels.description: Flat against a rising announce rate means the cluster is not pulling.

panels.title: Pull latency p99
panels.description: This sits on the cluster's block-validation critical path. A slow pull here is indistinguishable, cluster-side, from a slow peer.

panels.title: Chain-sync divert canary
panels.description: The cluster selecting the BRIDGE as a catchup source. Rare bursts accompany multi-peer degradation; a sustained rate means the synthetic peer-id no longer diverts catchup, and the next node to fall behind may wedge.

panels.title: Submit outcomes
panels.description: rejected = the cluster refusing on merits. failed = transport or server fault.

panels.title: Submit latency p99
panels.description: Labelled by outcome because 'slow' and 'refusing' are different faults with the same counter signature: a 429 in a millisecond and an accept in two seconds move the batch counter identically.

panels.title: Queue depth
panels.description: At the ceiling, backpressure blocks the lane read loop — which is the design, not a fault.

panels.title: Pipeline anomalies
panels.description: unattributed is the one to alert on: those transactions' outcome is UNKNOWN and excluded from accepted, so delivery counts are incomplete rather than merely bad.

panels.title: Skipped, by reason
panels.description: remote_origin and foreign_origin are the origin filter working as intended. standby is a bridge that does not hold the role. not_ready is the startup grace.

panels.title: Up-tunnel
panels.description: A climbing redial count tracks failures and means the ingress is flapping.

panels.title: Asset fetch p99
panels.description: Building an object from the cluster's asset service. A block assembled from many subtrees is not a millisecond operation.

panels.title: Up-tunnel write p99
panels.description: Includes time queued behind another object: one connection per class, so the writes serialise and the wait is time the reverse path is actually blocked.

panels.title: Freshness — what a flat counter cannot tell you
Time since last object
panels.description: Every bridge counter is monotonic, so a stalled lane, a dead edge and a quiet network all render as the same flat line. These gauges are seeded with the process start time, so the value is always an age.

panels.title: Time since last event
panels.description: The notification age ticks on PINGs too, so a live subscription on an idle chain stays low — which is what makes 'the subscription is dead' separable from 'the chain is quiet'.
